projects.title: Fibonacci Numbers (Memoization vs Tabulation vs Space Optimization O(1))
projects.description: Dynamic Programming (DP) optimizes recursive overlapping subproblems by storing computed results. Compare: 1) Memoization Top-Down `O(N)` time, `O(N)` memory; 2) Tabulation Bottom-Up `O(N)` time, `O(N)` array; 3) Space-Optimized DP `O(N)` time, `O(1)` memory using 2 variables! In this project, you will build Fibonacci 1D DP Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Overlapping Subproblems, Top-Down Memoization vs Bottom-Up Tabulation & O(1) Space Reduction
projects.exampleText: Compute Fibonacci(10) via space-optimized 1D DP
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Fibonacci 1D DP (Space Optimized O(1)) ---
Fibonacci(10) = 55
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Recurrence Relation**: `dp[i] = dp[i-1] + dp[i-2]`.
2. **Space Optimization**: Maintain `prev2` and `prev1`; update `curr = prev1 + prev2`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `fib_space_opt()`: Computes Fibonacci numbers using space-optimized 1D DP in O(1) memory.

projects.title: Climbing Stairs (1 or 2 Steps Step Counting DP)
projects.description: You are climbing a staircase of N steps. You can take either 1 step or 2 steps at a time. Find total distinct ways to reach the top. Recurrence relation `dp[i] = dp[i-1] + dp[i-2]` matches Fibonacci sequence! Solved in O(N) time and O(1) space. In this project, you will build Climbing Stairs DP Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Step Counting DP Patterns, Path Addition Recurrences & Fibonacci Reduction
projects.exampleText: Find ways to climb N=5 stairs
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Climbing Stairs (1D DP) ---
Ways to climb 5 stairs = 8
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Base Cases**: `dp[1] = 1, dp[2] = 2`.
2. **Step Addition**: `dp[i] = dp[i-1] + dp[i-2]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `climb_stairs()`: Solves Climbing Stairs using 1D DP in O(1) auxiliary space.

projects.title: Min Cost Climbing Stairs
projects.description: Given array `cost` where `cost[i]` is cost of step `i`, find minimum cost to reach top of staircase starting at step 0 or 1. Recurrence: `dp[i] = cost[i] + min(dp[i-1], dp[i-2])` in O(N) time and O(1) space! In this project, you will build Min Cost Climbing Stairs Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Cost Minimization DP Recurrences, Base State Selection & Constant Space DP
projects.exampleText: Find minimum cost to climb stairs for [10, 15, 20]
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Min Cost Climbing Stairs (1D DP) ---
Min Cost = 15
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Cost Recurrence**: `dp[i] = cost[i] + min(dp[i-1], dp[i-2])`.
2. **Top Reach**: Return `min(prev1, prev2)`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `min_cost_climbing_stairs()`: Solves Min Cost Climbing Stairs in O(N) time and O(1) space.

projects.title: House Robber I (Non-Adjacent Element Selection)
projects.description: Rob houses along a street without triggering alarms (cannot rob two adjacent houses). Find maximum money robbed. Decision at house `i`: either Rob House `i` (`nums[i] + dp[i-2]`) OR Skip House `i` (`dp[i-1]`). Recurrence: `dp[i] = max(dp[i-1], nums[i] + dp[i-2])` in O(N) time! In this project, you will build House Robber I Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Non-Adjacent Element Selection DP, Binary Choice Transitions (Rob vs Skip) & O(1) Memory
projects.exampleText: Rob maximum money from houses [2, 7, 9, 3, 1]
projects.exampleOutput:
--- House Robber I (1D DP) ---
Maximum Robbed Value = 12
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Choice Rule**: `curr = max(prev1, prev2 + nums[i])`.
2. **State Updates**: `prev2 = prev1; prev1 = curr`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `rob_house()`: Solves House Robber I using space-optimized 1D DP.

projects.title: House Robber II (Circular Array Non-Adjacent DP)
projects.description: Houses are arranged in a CIRCLE (first house and last house are adjacent). Since house 0 and house N-1 cannot be robbed together, run House Robber I twice: 1) Range `0 .. N-2`; 2) Range `1 .. N-1`. Return `max(range1, range2)` in O(N) time! In this project, you will build House Robber II Circular Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Circular Array Constraints, Boundary Split Range DP & Maximization Over Cases
projects.exampleText: Find max robbed value in circular houses
projects.exampleOutput:
--- House Robber II (Circular Array 1D DP) ---
Maximum Robbed Value in Circular Houses = 11
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Range Split**: Run House Robber DP on `nums[0..N-2]` and `nums[1..N-1]`.
2. **Circular Maximum**: Return `max(rob(0..N-2), rob(1..N-1))`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `house_robber_ii_demo()`: Solves House Robber II for circular arrays.

projects.title: Maximum Product Subarray (Tracking Min/Max Products)
projects.description: Find contiguous subarray with maximum product. Negative numbers can flip a tiny minimum product into a huge positive maximum product! Maintain TWO dynamic states at step `i`: `max_prod` AND `min_prod`. When `nums[i] < 0`, swap `max_prod` and `min_prod` in O(N) time! In this project, you will build Max Product Subarray Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Dual Min/Max Product Tracking, Negative Factor Swaps & Dynamic Subarray Maxima
projects.exampleText: Find maximum product subarray
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Maximum Product Subarray (Min/Max Tracking 1D DP) ---
Maximum Product Subarray = 6
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Negative Swap**: Swap `max_p` and `min_p` when `nums[i] < 0`.
2. **State Recurrence**: `max_p = max(nums[i], max_p * nums[i])`, `min_p = min(nums[i], min_p * nums[i])`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `max_product_subarray_demo()`: Computes maximum product subarray using dual DP state tracking.

projects.title: Coin Change I (Minimum Coins for Target Sum)
projects.description: Given coins array and target amount, find FEWEST coins needed to make up amount. Dynamic Programming recurrence: `dp[i] = min(dp[i], 1 + dp[i - coin])` for all coins. Returns minimum coins in `O(N * Target)` time! In this project, you will build Coin Change I Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Unbounded Knapsack Minimization, Coin Recurrence Transitions & Target Sum DP
projects.exampleText: Find minimum coins for target amount 11
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Coin Change I (Minimum Coins 1D DP) ---
Minimum Coins required for target 11 = 3
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **DP Array**: `dp[0] = 0`, all other `dp[i] = INF`.
2. **Min Recurrence**: `dp[i] = min(dp[i], 1 + dp[i - c])` for `c` in coins.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `coin_change_i_demo()`: Solves Coin Change I minimum coins using 1D DP.

projects.title: Coin Change II (Total Combination Ways to Make Change)
projects.description: Find total number of UNIQUE combinations to make up target amount using coins array. Outer loop iterates over COINS, inner loop iterates over AMOUNT `i = coin .. target`: `dp[i] += dp[i - coin]`. Ensures combination ordering without duplicate permutations! In this project, you will build Coin Change II Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Unbounded Knapsack Combinations, Outer Coin Iteration & Permutation Avoidance
projects.exampleText: Find total combination ways to make amount 5
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Coin Change II (Total Combinations 1D DP) ---
Total Combination Ways to make amount 5 = 4
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Outer Coin Loop**: Iterate `coin` on outer loop to count combinations (unordered sets).
2. **Combination Accumulation**: `dp[i] += dp[i - coin]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `coin_change_ii_demo()`: Solves Coin Change II total combinations using 1D DP.

projects.title: Decode Ways (A-Z Number Sequence Message Decoding)
projects.description: Message encoded using 'A'->1 .. 'Z'->26. Given numeric string s, find total ways to decode it. At position `i`: 1) Single digit `s[i-1]` (1..9): `dp[i] += dp[i-1]`; 2) Double digit `s[i-2..i-1]` (10..26): `dp[i] += dp[i-2]`. Solved in O(N) time! In this project, you will build Decode Ways Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Sequence Decoding DP, Valid Numeric Range Invariants (1..9, 10..26) & Subproblem Sums
projects.exampleText: Find valid decoding ways for string '226'
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Decode Ways (Message Sequence 1D DP) ---
Total Valid Decoding Ways for '226' = 3
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Single Digit Test**: If `s[i-1] != '0'`, add `dp[i-1]`.
2. **Two Digit Test**: If two-digit number `10..26`, add `dp[i-2]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `decode_ways_demo()`: Solves Decode Ways message decoding using 1D DP.

projects.title: Word Break I (Dictionary Word Segmenting)
projects.description: Given string s and dictionary of words, determine if s can be segmented into space-separated dictionary words. DP state `dp[i]` is true if substring `s[0..i-1]` can be segmented into valid words: `dp[i] = dp[j] && wordDict.contains(s[j..i])`. In this project, you will build Word Break I Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: String Partition DP, Substring Dictionary Lookups & Boolean Array Transitions
projects.exampleText: Verify dictionary segmentation for 'leetcode'
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Word Break I (Dictionary Segmenting 1D DP) ---
Can segment 'leetcode' into dictionary words: YES
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Subproblem Partition**: `dp[i]` tests all cut points `j < i`.
2. **Dictionary Check**: `dp[i] = dp[j] && contains(s[j..i-1])`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `word_break_demo()`: Solves Word Break I using 1D DP.

projects.title: Longest Increasing Subsequence (LIS) in O(N^2) & O(N log N)
projects.description: Find length of Longest Increasing Subsequence (LIS). 1) Standard 1D DP `dp[i] = 1 + max(dp[j])` runs in `O(N^2)` time; 2) Patience Sorting with Binary Search (`tails` array) runs in optimal `O(N log N)` time! In this project, you will build LIS 1D DP Solver in C.
projects.learningOutcome: LIS DP Formulation `O(N^2)` vs Binary Search Patience Sorting `O(N log N)` Optimization
projects.exampleText: Compute LIS length for [10, 9, 2, 5, 3, 7, 101, 18]
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Longest Increasing Subsequence (LIS 1D DP) ---
LIS Length for [10, 9, 2, 5, 3, 7, 101, 18] = 4
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **O(N^2) DP**: `dp[i] = 1 + max(dp[j])` for all `j < i` where `nums[j] < nums[i]`.
2. **O(N log N) Patience Sorting**: Maintain `tails` array; binary search `lower_bound` location for `nums[i]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `lis_1d_dp_demo()`: Solves LIS in O(N^2) and O(N log N) time.

projects.title: Partition Equal Subset Sum
projects.description: Determine if array can be partitioned into two subsets with equal sum. If `total_sum` is odd, return false. Find if subset sum `target = total_sum / 2` exists using 1D Bitset/Boolean DP `dp[i] |= dp[i - num]` in O(N * Target) time! In this project, you will build Subset Sum Partition Solver in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Subset Sum 1D DP, Target Halving & Reverse Space Iteration (0-1 Knapsack)
projects.exampleText: Partition array [1, 5, 11, 5] into two equal sum subsets
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Partition Equal Subset Sum (1D DP) ---
Can partition array [1, 5, 11, 5] into two equal sum subsets: YES
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Target Calculation**: `target = total_sum / 2`.
2. **Reverse 1D Loop**: Loop `i` from `target` down to `num`: `dp[i] = dp[i] || dp[i - num]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `partition_equal_subset_sum_demo()`: Solves Partition Equal Subset Sum using 1D DP.

projects.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock with Cooldown
projects.description: Find maximum stock profit with 1-day cooldown after selling a stock. Maintain 3 State DP variables: 1) `hold` (currently owning stock); 2) `sold` (just sold stock today); 3) `rest` (cooldown or inactive). Update states in O(N) time! In this project, you will build Stock Trading Cooldown DP Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: State Machine Dynamic Programming, Multi-State Transitions & Cooldown Invariants
projects.exampleText: Calculate maximum stock profit with 1-day cooldown
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Stock Trading with Cooldown (State Machine 1D DP) ---
Maximum Profit with 1-day Cooldown = 3
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Hold State**: `hold = max(prev_hold, prev_rest - price)`.
2. **Sold State**: `sold = prev_hold + price`.
3. **Rest State**: `rest = max(prev_rest, prev_sold)`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `stock_cooldown_demo()`: Solves Stock Trading with Cooldown using State Machine 1D DP.

projects.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock with Transaction Fee
projects.description: Find maximum stock profit when every transaction incurs a fixed fee. Maintain 2 State DP variables: `hold` (owning stock) and `free` (not owning stock). Update `free = max(free, hold + price - fee)` in O(N) time and O(1) space! In this project, you will build Stock Fee DP Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Transaction Fee Deductions, 2-State DP Invariants & Constant Space Profits
projects.exampleText: Calculate maximum stock profit with transaction fee
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Stock Trading with Transaction Fee (1D DP) ---
Maximum Profit with Transaction Fee = 8
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Hold Transition**: `hold = max(hold, free - price)`.
2. **Free Transition**: `free = max(free, hold + price - fee)`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `stock_transaction_fee_demo()`: Solves Stock Trading with Transaction Fee using 1D DP.

projects.title: Perfect Squares (Lagrange's 4-Square DP)
projects.description: Find minimum number of perfect square numbers (1, 4, 9, 16...) that sum to N. Recurrence: `dp[i] = min(dp[i], 1 + dp[i - j*j])` for all `j*j <= i`. Solved in `O(N sqrt(N))` time! In this project, you will build Perfect Squares 1D DP Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Lagrange's Four-Square Theorem, Square Subproblem Recurrences & Min Reduction
projects.exampleText: Find minimum perfect squares summing to N=12
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Perfect Squares (Lagrange's 4-Square 1D DP) ---
Minimum Perfect Squares summing to 12 = 3 (4 + 4 + 4)
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Base Case**: `dp[0] = 0`.
2. **Square Loop**: `dp[i] = min(dp[i], 1 + dp[i - j*j])` for `j*j <= i`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `perfect_squares_demo()`: Solves Perfect Squares problem using 1D DP.

projects.title: Integer Break (Maximizing Product of Sum Parts)
projects.description: Given integer N, break it into sum of at least two positive integers and maximize the product of those integers. Recurrence: `dp[i] = max(dp[i], max(j * (i - j), j * dp[i - j]))`. Solved in `O(N^2)` time! In this project, you will build Integer Break Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Integer Product Maximization, Subproblem Splitting & Dynamic Multiplication
projects.exampleText: Maximize product for integer N=10
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Integer Break (Maximizing Product of Sum Parts) ---
Maximum Product for integer N=10 = 36 (3 * 3 * 4)
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Cut Choice**: Split `i` into `j` and `i - j`.
2. **Max Product**: `max(j * (i - j), j * dp[i - j])`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `integer_break_demo()`: Solves Integer Break maximizing product of sum parts using 1D DP.

projects.title: Combination Sum IV (Permutation Ordering DP)
projects.description: Given distinct integers array and target, find number of possible PERMUTATION combinations that add up to target (where different orderings count as distinct). Outer loop iterates over TARGET `i = 1 .. target`, inner loop iterates over NUMS: `dp[i] += dp[i - num]`. Solved in `O(N * Target)` time! In this project, you will build Combination Sum IV Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Permutation Ordering DP, Outer Target Iteration & Combination Sum Invariants
projects.exampleText: Find total permutation combinations for target 4
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Combination Sum IV (Permutation Ordering 1D DP) ---
Total Permutation Combinations for target 4 = 7
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Outer Target Loop**: Iterate `target` on outer loop to count permutations (ordered sets).
2. **Permutation Accumulation**: `dp[i] += dp[i - num]` for `num <= i`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `combination_sum_iv_demo()`: Solves Combination Sum IV permutation ordering using 1D DP.

projects.title: Push Dominoes (Linear State Invariant Mechanics)
projects.description: Dominoes standing vertically can fall to left 'L' or right 'R'. Compute final state of dominoes array. Calculate rightward forces `force[i]` in left-to-right pass, and leftward forces in right-to-left pass. Net force determines final domino tilt in O(N) time! In this project, you will build Push Dominoes Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Two-Pass Force Sweeps, Net State Invariants & Linear Array Physics Simulation
projects.exampleText: Simulate final state of dominoes string
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Push Dominoes (Linear State Invariants) ---
Final Dominoes State: 'LL.RR.LLRRRR'
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Left-to-Right Force**: Propagate decreasing positive force for 'R'.
2. **Right-to-Left Force**: Propagate decreasing negative force for 'L'. Compare net force.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `push_dominoes_demo()`: Solves Push Dominoes using 2-pass linear state DP.

projects.title: Count Number of Teams (Triplets DP Invariant)
projects.description: Given soldiers rating array, count total valid teams of 3 soldiers `(i, j, k)` with ratings strictly increasing `rating[i] < rating[j] < rating[k]` or decreasing. For each middle soldier `j`, count smaller/larger soldiers to left and right in O(N^2) time! In this project, you will build Count Number of Teams Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Middle Element Anchoring, Left/Right Combination Products & Triplet Counting
projects.exampleText: Count valid 3-soldier teams
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Count Number of Teams (Triplets 1D DP Invariants) ---
Total Valid Teams Count = 3
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Anchor Middle Soldier j**: Count `left_less`, `left_more`, `right_less`, `right_more`.
2. **Team Combinations**: `teams += (left_less * right_more) + (left_more * right_less)`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `count_teams_demo()`: Solves Count Number of Teams using middle element anchoring.

projects.title: Frog Jump (K-Step Variable Distance Hop DP)
projects.description: A frog is attempting to cross a river by jumping on stones. If frog's last jump was K units, its next jump MUST be `K-1`, `K`, or `K+1` units. Determine if frog can reach last stone. DP state `dp[stone_idx]` stores set of valid jump distances K in `O(N^2)` time! In this project, you will build Frog Jump Solver in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Variable Hop Distance DP, HashSet/Bitmask State Storage & Dynamic Jump Validation
projects.exampleText: Verify frog jump reachability to last stone
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Frog Jump (K-Step Variable Distance Hop DP) ---
Can Frog reach last stone: YES
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Jump Set**: `dp[i]` holds all jump lengths `K` that reach stone `i`.
2. **3-Way Hop**: Try next jumps `K-1`, `K`, and `K+1` from stone `i`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `frog_jump_demo()`: Solves Frog Jump variable hop problem using 1D DP.

projects.title: Matrix Exponentiation Engine for Linear DP Recurrences in O(K^3 log N)
projects.description: Compute N-th term of ANY linear DP recurrence (e.g. Fibonacci, Tribonacci, Tile Covering) for huge N up to 10^18 in logarithmic `O(K^3 log N)` time using Matrix Fast Exponentiation! In this project, you will build Matrix Exponentiation DP Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Matrix Exponentiation, Linear DP State Transformation Matrices & O(K^3 log N) Powering
projects.exampleText: Compute N-th linear DP recurrence term for N=10^18
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Matrix Exponentiation Engine for Linear DP Recurrences ---
Computed N-th Recurrence Term for N=10^18 in O(K^3 log N) time.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Transformation Matrix**: Construct K x K transition matrix `M`.
2. **Binary Matrix Exponentiation**: Compute `M^N` using binary powering in `O(K^3 log N)`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `matrix_exponentiation_dp_demo()`: Solves linear DP recurrences in O(K^3 log N) using Matrix Exponentiation.

projects.title: Convex Hull Trick (CHT) & Line Container DP Optimization in O(N)
projects.description: When 1D DP transition formulas take the form `dp[i] = min(m_j * x_i + c_j)`, naive calculation takes O(N^2). The Convex Hull Trick (CHT) maintains lower envelope lines `y = m * x + c` in a deque, optimizing transition time down to linear `O(N)`! In this project, you will build CHT DP Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Convex Hull Trick (CHT), Line Container Envelopes & O(N^2) to O(N) DP Acceleration
projects.exampleText: Optimize 1D DP transition from O(N^2) to O(N) via CHT
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Convex Hull Trick (CHT) & Line Container DP Optimization ---
Optimized 1D DP transition time from O(N^2) down to linear O(N) using CHT.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Line Geometry**: Model DP transitions as linear equations `y = m*x + c`.
2. **Deque Pruning**: Prune redundant lines whose intersection points fall outside optimal range.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `convex_hull_trick_demo()`: Solves Convex Hull Trick 1D DP optimization.

projects.title: Divide & Conquer DP Optimization for Monotonic Transitions
projects.description: When DP optimal transition indices `opt[i][j]` satisfy monotonicity `opt[i][j] <= opt[i][j+1]`, Divide & Conquer DP Optimization reduces time complexity from `O(K N^2)` down to `O(K N log N)`! In this project, you will build Divide & Conquer DP Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Divide & Conquer DP Optimization, Monotonic Transition Proofs & O(K N log N) Speedup
projects.exampleText: Optimize DP transitions from O(K N^2) to O(K N log N)
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Divide & Conquer DP Optimization for Monotonic Transitions ---
Optimized 2D/1D DP transitions from O(K N^2) down to O(K N log N) using D&C DP.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Monotonicity Rule**: `opt[i][j]` increases monotonically with `j`.
2. **D&C Recursion**: Solve midpoint `mid`; search optimal cut ONLY in range `[opt_left, opt_right]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `divide_conquer_dp_demo()`: Solves Divide & Conquer DP optimization for monotonic transitions.

projects.title: Parallel SIMD Vectorized 1D DP State Machine Kernel
projects.description: Accelerate 1D DP state machine transitions across massive datasets using 256-bit AVX2 SIMD vector instructions, evaluating 8 DP state updates simultaneously in 1 CPU clock cycle! In this project, you will build SIMD 1D DP Kernel in C.
projects.learningOutcome: SIMD AVX2 1D DP Vectorization, Parallel State Transitions & Vector Register Min/Max
projects.exampleText: Evaluate 8 parallel 1D DP state transitions in 256-bit AVX2 registers
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Parallel SIMD Vectorized 1D DP State Machine Kernel ---
Evaluated 8 parallel 1D DP state transitions in 256-bit AVX2 registers.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Vector Register**: Load 8 1D DP subproblem values into 256-bit AVX2 register.
2. **SIMD Vector Pass**: Compute 8 SIMD DP transitions in single CPU clock cycle.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `simd_1d_dp_demo()`: Simulates SIMD vectorized 1D DP state machine kernel.

projects.title: High-Throughput Memory-Mapped Real-Time Telemetry DP Predictor
projects.description: High-frequency trading and IoT telemetry engines evaluate 10,000,000 streaming 1D DP predictions per second over memory-mapped shared memory buffers (`mmap`) with zero latency overhead. In this project, you will build Real-Time Telemetry DP Predictor in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Memory-Mapped DP Buffers, 10M Stream DP Predictions & High-Frequency Engine
projects.exampleText: Evaluate 10M streaming telemetry DP predictions/sec
projects.exampleOutput:
--- High-Throughput Memory-Mapped Real-Time Telemetry DP Predictor ---
Evaluated 10,000,000 streaming telemetry DP predictions per second.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Memory-Mapped State**: Store 1D DP state arrays in shared memory mapped virtual space.
2. **Microsecond Predictions**: Execute zero-copy DP state transitions directly from RAM offsets.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `stream_telemetry_dp_demo()`: Simulates high-throughput memory-mapped real-time telemetry DP predictor.
